 ZH KR Zetta Hannany, Kholid Rafsanjani 22 October 2026, 14:40 WIB ZH Zetta Hannany Reporter KR Kholid Rafsanjani Reporter WhatsApp Channel Bahlil considers ending gas export contracts to neighbouring countries to safeguard energy supplies. JAKARTA – Energy and Mineral Resources Minister Bahlil Lahadalia has opened the possibility of Indonesia terminating gas export contracts with neighbouring countries.
 Bahlil made the statement after attending a plenary cabinet meeting at the State Palace in Jakarta on Wednesday evening (21/10), marking the second anniversary of President Prabowo Subianto's administration.
 According to Bahlil, the option is being considered in response to Prabowo's directive amid global geopolitical developments that require Indonesia to enter a “survival” phase.
 Bahlil stressed that all ministries must prioritise meeting domestic supply needs before sending energy commodities abroad. “I may consider not extending gas export contracts with neighbouring countries, because we have to ‘survive’ by meeting domestic needs,” he said.
 Read Also: MUFG warns of MSCI impact on rupiah after BI holds rates Bahlil also warned other countries against underestimating Indonesia. “So if other countries have a different view of us, they should be careful,” he said, without specifying which countries he was referring to.
 However, the statement comes amid pressure on Indonesia from several countries.
 President Prabowo also emphasised the importance of bureaucratic efficiency in strategic decision-making in the energy sector. “The key is to work quickly and execute quickly, not slowly, in accordance with the rules and without violating them,” Bahlil stressed.
 The remarks come amid various external parties' comments on Indonesia's domestic situation, ranging from the handling of forest and land fires to capital market reform.
 As reported by IDNFinancials.com , the Malaysian parliament recently urged ASEAN to hold parties responsible for transboundary haze accountable.
 Meanwhile, in the capital market, Singapore was suspected of intervening with global index provider MSCI to push for Indonesia's market classification to be downgraded to Standalone Market status, alongside Zimbabwe and Argentina . Singapore subsequently issued an official statement denying the allegation.
 According to government data, Indonesia supplied thousands of tonnes of gas to several neighbouring countries throughout 2025. These included Japan, with 3,798 tonnes; China, with 3,789 tonnes; Singapore, with 3,547 tonnes; and South Korea, with 2,269 tonnes. (KR/ZH)
